entries.title: DRAFT: Conditional averaging can amplify Sobolev energy
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent w353 proof check pending. For p>=2, start with joint density proportional to exp(-x) on x>=|y|^p. Let sigma^2=Gamma(3/p)/Gamma(1/p), U=(X-1-1/p)/sqrt(1+1/p), V=Y/sigma. The resulting law is centered isotropic and log-concave. The author derivation for f(u,v)=u gives input gradient energy 1 and conditional-mean gradient energy D_p=p^2 Gamma(3/p) Gamma(2-1/p)/[(1+1/p) Gamma(1/p)^2], with D_p/p tending to 1/3. This candidate obstruction concerns a uniform Sobolev bound for conditional averaging, not the KLS conclusion. The conditional mean variance is 1/(p+1).

entries.title: DRAFT: Balanced block variance comparison loses a linear dimension factor
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent w353 proof check pending. Let n=2d, d>=1, and X=(U,V) be uniform on the Euclidean ball of radius sqrt(n+2) in R^n, split into orthogonal d-dimensional blocks. This law is centered isotropic and log-concave. For f=|U|^2-|V|^2 the author derivation gives Var(f)=2n(n+2)/(n+4), E|grad f|^2=4n, and Var(f)/[E Var(f|U)+E Var(f|V)]=(n+4)/4. Maximal block correlation is at least n/(n+4). A dimension-uniform conditional-variance comparison for every balanced split therefore requires hypotheses beyond isotropic log-concavity. This does not refute KLS or an unbalanced splitting strategy.

relations.rationale: The first endpoint gives the draft comparison factor (n+4)/4; the second gives the draft conditional gradient energy D_p/p -> 1/3. These are distinct obstructions to a conditioning proof mechanism. Neither endpoint states that KLS is false.
